Container.Name: Beltr
Container.Overview:
CPU BUILD: runs on any server, no GPU needed. If your box has an NVIDIA card or Intel graphics, install Beltr-NVIDIA or Beltr-Intel instead: same app, much faster song processing.
Beltr turns any song in your music library into a karaoke track. It separates the vocals out with a local AI model, finds synced lyrics online (or drafts them locally when no provider has the song), force-aligns them to the vocal word by word, and displays them on a TV while everyone's phone acts as a remote — scan the QR code on screen, no app to install.
Everything runs on your server. Nothing about your library is uploaded.
FIRST RUN: Beltr downloads about 2 GB of model weights into /cache the first time it needs them. That happens once and survives container updates as long as /cache stays mapped. Watch the container log if a first song seems to sit still — the download is what it's doing.
SPEED: this is the CPU image. On a modern multi-core server, separating a 3-4 minute song takes a few minutes; most songs then get their lyrics instantly from an online lyrics database. The slow case is a song no lyrics provider knows, which falls back to local transcription and can take a couple of minutes. If your server has an NVIDIA GPU, install "Beltr-NVIDIA" instead; it is dramatically faster. An Intel processor with integrated graphics (6th gen Core onward, N100 included) or an Arc A-series card can use "Beltr-Intel". AMD GPUs are not supported in the container.
LICENSE: Beltr is a one-time purchase (no subscription). Run it free for five songs, then enter your key from beltr.app in the License key field below — or drop it in a file at /config/license.key. It activates once and then works offline. Container updates and restarts do not re-activate, as long as you keep the Config path mapped; a key covers two installs.
AFTER INSTALL: open the WebUI, go to Settings, and add /media as a music folder. Then open http://your-server:8477/tv on whatever screen you're singing at, and scan the QR with a phone.
MICROPHONES NEED HTTPS: browsers only allow microphone access on a secure page. Beltr serves one itself on port 8478 with a self-signed certificate: open https://your-server:8478/tv on the laptop or phone that has the microphone and accept the browser's warning once. Everything else — queueing, playback, lyrics, stem mixing, the QR the TV shows — works over plain http on 8477. A reverse proxy with a real certificate is only needed if you want no warning at all.
NOTE: Beltr assumes everyone who can reach it is trusted. Set AUTH_PASSWORD to put a password on the TV and dashboard screens, but do not expose this container to the internet without a reverse proxy doing real authentication in front of it.

Container.Changes:
### 2026-09-01
Overview text only: describes the lyrics pipeline accurately (online lookup or local draft, then forced alignment) and names the Beltr-Intel sibling. No config, path or variable changes.
### 2026-08-14
First Community Applications release. The container tracks the Beltr desktop release line — per-version notes are at https://github.com/CasaVargas/beltr-releases/releases
Container.Requires: Internet access on first start to activate a license key (or to begin the five-song trial). After that Beltr keeps working offline.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the web interface, the TV screen and the phone remotes. Change the host side only if 8477 is already taken.

Config.Name: HTTPS Port
Config.Description: Self-signed HTTPS for microphones (browsers only allow the mic on a secure page). Open https://your-server:8478/tv on the device with the mic and accept the warning once. Keep host and container sides equal: Beltr builds the address it shows from this number.

Config.Name: HTTPS
Config.Description: on = also serve https on the HTTPS Port with a self-signed certificate Beltr generates and keeps in /config/tls. off = plain http only (microphones then need a reverse proxy with a certificate).

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: App state: database, settings, logs, lyrics. Small and written often — keep it on appdata (SSD/cache pool).

Config.Name: Library
Config.Description: Processed karaoke library: separated stems and imported audio. Roughly 60-120 MB per song, so point this at the array, NOT at appdata.

Config.Name: Music (read-only)
Config.Description: Your existing music. Mounted read-only — Beltr copies what it imports and never writes here. Add it as a music folder in Settings after the first start.

Config.Name: Model cache
Config.Description: Downloaded AI model weights, about 2 GB. Keep this mapped or every container update re-downloads them. Faster storage makes model loading quicker.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID that owns the files Beltr writes. 99 (nobody) is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID that owns the files Beltr writes. 100 (users) is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone, e.g. America/New_York. Affects log timestamps.

Config.Name: License key
Config.Description: Your key from beltr.app. Activates once against this install and then works offline — updating or recreating the container does not re-activate, as long as you keep the Config path. Leave blank to try Beltr free: five songs, then it asks you to buy. You can also put the key in a file at /config/license.key instead.

Config.Name: Host PIN
Config.Description: Six digits that unlock host controls on a phone (skip, reorder, delete). Leave blank and Beltr picks a random one on every start, which changes if the container restarts mid-party.

Config.Name: Host password
Config.Description: Optional password on the TV and dashboard screens and the settings endpoints. Phones joining a room are NOT affected. This keeps the household out of your settings; it is not internet-grade authentication.

Config.Name: Fix permissions
Config.Description: first-run: fix ownership once, then only the top-level folders. always: fix everything on every start (slow on a big library). never: leave ownership alone.
